task: For this synthetic writing exercise, use the fictional reporting notes to write a straight news story for a general newspaper audience. Write from this reporting snapshot as of April 7, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Harwick State Attorney General Carla Muñoz filed an antitrust lawsuit Monday, April 7, 2025, in U.S. District Court for the District of Harwick against Nexum Technologies.
The complaint alleges Nexum violated Sections 1 and 2 of the Sherman Antitrust Act by requiring app stores to process all in-app purchases exclusively through Nexum's payment system.
Muñoz said: "Our investigation found a deliberate strategy to block smaller processors from competing on the merits."
Nexum spokesperson Paul Sterling said the claims "misread our contracts and misunderstand how competitive payment markets actually work" and said the company would defend the case vigorously.
The complaint seeks injunctive relief to void the exclusive dealing contracts and $500 million in monetary relief for affected consumers; no court has ruled on the requested remedies.
Nexum holds approximately 67 percent of the mobile payment processing market in Harwick State, according to the complaint's market-share analysis.
The lawsuit was triggered in part by a complaint filed by ClearPay Inc., a small Harwick-based payment processor.
ClearPay CEO Amanda Jin said her company had "lost five signed partnership agreements after Nexum applied pressure on our distribution partners."
Harwick is filing the lawsuit alone; the U.S. Department of Justice said through a spokesperson it is "monitoring the litigation" but has not joined the case.
The Federal Trade Commission closed a 2022 investigation into Nexum's app store practices without bringing an enforcement action; the packet supplies no finding that the conduct was lawful.
Nexum processed approximately $4.1 billion in mobile payment transactions in Harwick State in 2024, according to the complaint.
The state's expert economist calculated approximately $380 million in "supracompetitive" payment-processing fees between 2020 and 2024.
The complaint identifies six app store operators as parties to the exclusive contracts; none are named as defendants.

Daniel Trent, an antitrust professor at fictional Fairhaven Law School who is not involved in the case, described the legal theory as plausible but said exclusive dealing claims in digital markets can be difficult to prove.
Nexum's stock fell 3.8 percent Monday following news of the lawsuit.
The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge Harriet Fontaine.
Nexum employs approximately 2,400 people, including a Harwick State office of roughly 300 employees.
The complaint was developed over 18 months of investigation by Muñoz's office.
Muñoz's office said the state's investigation included review of more than 400,000 pages of internal company documents produced under civil investigative demand.
The six app stores named in the contracts include both large national platforms and regional operators, according to the complaint; Muñoz's office declined to identify them by name.
